subject: barney
label: barney, in the place of the game's models/barney.mdl

measured.lineup: the asset is one of A to D in lineup.png beside models/hassassin.mdl, models/scientist.mdl, models/gman.mdl
measured.lineupTest: asked 4 times, each in another order, which of the four was not made by Valve: judges picked C, D, C, D where the asset was A, C, C, B: passed for one of the game's

M1.reason: Outline matches the brief's words: an upright man with a rounded visored helmet, a bulky vest over a short-sleeved shirt, a holster at the hip and boots. In the front, back and side views no part sticks out or is missing. The forward-bent arm in the side views is a pose, not a fault.

M2.reason: Measured size 29.4 x 24.4 x 76.1 against the 75 asked: height is 1.4% off, inside the 15% band.

M3.reason: Named parts are all there: the helmet with its dark front visor, the black vest, the blue shirt, the blue-violet trousers, the pistol holster at the right hip (visible in front-left and back-right), and hands and boots. The SECURITY lettering is on the front, not the back as the brief asks, but it is paint, so it is charged to M5, not to a missing part.

M4.reason: Regions have the brief's colours: a bright blue shirt and sleeves, blue-violet trousers, a black vest, skin-toned hands and black boots. Nothing reads as a wrong material.

M5.reason: The brief puts SECURITY on the back of the vest, but the lettering is only on the front (front and front-left views); the back view shows a plain black vest. The trousers also carry a heavy grainy speckle that the brief does not ask for. That is a marking in the wrong place and extra grain, both paint faults.

M6.reason: Capped by the line-up test as instructed. The asset was picked as the non-Valve model once in four readings (picked at C, D, C, D against the asset at A, C, C, B), below the twice-in-four that would cap it at 1.

M7.reason: The front is the front: the SECURITY lettering and visor face forward, the figure stands upright on its boots, and the feet rest on the floor line in every side view.

M8.reason: SMAK's check reports no errors. At 650 triangles it is under twice the median (504, so 1008) and under the third quartile (731). Nothing visible is open, inside out or floating; the underside view shows the boots and hand as solid pieces.

C1.reason: Through the 22-frame run and the 7-frame two-hand attack, the head, vest, arms, holster and boots stay on the body and move with it. The vest and back pouch shift a little with the stride, as the body does, and nothing comes apart, sinks or floats. The pictures are small, so this is a close-enough reading, not a pixel check.
